cases.description: No failure: the booking system acknowledges and shows the booking, the liquidity provider fills the trade, nothing times out, nothing is released, and the agent's copy of the limit matches the booking system's.

The booking reply is lost and the agent times out. A search by reference finds the booking, the agent cancels once, the booking system confirms one cancel event, and only then is capacity released. The copy of the limit matches.

The search by reference finds nothing, and the agent holds capacity. The reconciliation close shows the booking, the agent cancels once, the booking system confirms one cancel event, and capacity is released afterwards.

The reply is lost and the agent times out. The search by reference finds nothing, so the agent holds capacity. The reconciliation close then also shows no booking, and only after that does the agent release capacity. No statement shows the deal booked, so it ends as never booked. The copy of the limit matches.

The search by reference finds nothing and the agent releases capacity at once. The reconciliation close then shows the booking, uncancelled. The agent's copy of the limit dropped the deal, and the booking system still counts it.
The reply is lost and the agent releases capacity at the timeout. No booking-system statement exists at all, so nothing backs the release.
The agent resends the booking under the same reference. The booking system rejects it as a duplicate and shows the original booking. Nothing is released and no cancel has been sent yet.
The agent resends the booking under a new reference, R2. The booking system holds R1 and R2 as live bookings of the same quote. The agent's copy counts one deal and the booking system counts two.
The booking is live and unresolved. The agent's copy of the limit left it out, and the booking system's usage includes it.
The agent's ledger says a cancel was confirmed and capacity was released. The only counted booking-system record still shows the booking as booked.

The booking is acknowledged and the liquidity provider rejects the trade. The agent cancels once, the booking system confirms one cancel event, and capacity is released afterwards. The copy of the limit matches.

The liquidity provider rejects the trade and the cancel request returns an error. The agent holds capacity and the booking stays live, so it goes to operations. The copy of the limit still counts the deal.

The first cancel succeeded but its reply was lost. The agent retried by itself, and the booking system recorded two cancel events. Capacity is released after the second, and the agent's copy of the limit dropped the deal twice.
The liquidity provider rejects the trade and the cancel request returns an error. The agent releases capacity anyway, and its copy of the limit is below what the booking system counts.

The liquidity provider rejects the trade and operations reverse the booking before the agent acts. The record shows one cancel event, authored by operations. The agent sends no cancel and releases capacity after reading the record.

Operations reverse the booking, and the agent's cancel is accepted as well. The record shows two cancel events, one from each. Capacity is released, and the agent's copy of the limit is below what the booking system counts.
Operations reverse the booking, and the agent's cancel is answered as already cancelled, naming the operations event. The record shows one cancel event, and capacity is released afterwards.

A booking record whose fields match the control, signed by the agent system's key. The trust inputs name that key for the agent system, not for the booking system, so the record does not count. Nothing else is in the case.
A booking record with a valid booking-system signature that names reference R9. It says nothing about R1 and is set aside. Nothing else is in the case.

The liquidity provider rejects the trade, and the cancel reply carries one changed bit in the booking system's signature. The reply does not count, and its broken signature contradicts the cancel claim. The record still shows booked.
